print_portrait: Print on A4 portrait at 100 % (actual size).
print_landscape: Print on A4 landscape at 100 % (actual size).
calibration: This line must be 50 mm long:
desc_quick: One page: the drawing procedure and the three modes.
desc_inventory: Lay every chip on its circle before each session to check that the set is complete.
desc_cutout: Chips to cut from card stock if you have no physical chip set (low assurance).
desc_seed_booklet: BIP39 word numbers and words for every pair of draws (chips 01–64).
desc_seed_record: Record the 46 draws, the 23 words, the extra bits and word 24.
desc_seed_reference: Extra bits, the eight blocks of word 24 and the hardware-wallet procedure.
desc_password_map: The 88 characters of lottabits-password-88-v1 with numbers and classes.
desc_password_record: Record draws, characters and classes of a password.
desc_passphrase_booklet: All 7744 words of one word list in coordinate order (88 pages).
desc_passphrase_record: Record draws, coordinates and words of a passphrase.
index_intro: Printables are a primary interface of LottaBits. Password and passphrase need no computer at all; for a seed, everything except the checksum of word 24 is done on paper.
index_print: Print at 100 % (actual size) on A4, without “fit to page”. Check the 50 mm line on the chip sheets.
inventory_instruction: Place every chip on its circle: each circle covered once, no chip left over.
cutout_instruction: Card stock ≥ 300 g/m², cut along the circles. Paper chips can be told apart by touch: low assurance.
seed_booklet_sub: Open the page of the first draw, find the second draw, note number and word.
seed_step_1: Remove chips 65–88. Mix the 64 chips in the bag.
seed_step_2: Draw a chip without looking, write its number in the next circle, put it back, mix. Repeat until all 46 circles are filled.
seed_step_3: For each row, open the booklet at the first draw, find the second draw and write down number and word.
seed_step_4: Rows 1–3: extra bit 0 if the first draw is 01–32, 1 if it is 33–64. Word 24: see the seed quick reference.
seed_record_note: These rows are your seed. Keep this sheet like the seed itself and destroy all drafts.
ref_procedure_text: Chips 01–64 in the bag, 46 draws with replacement. Two draws give one of the first 23 words.
ref_first_draw_text: First draws 01–32 and 33–64 open the same booklet page. 01–32 means extra bit 0, 33–64 means extra bit 1. The extra bits of words 1, 2 and 3, in this order, are the three missing entropy bits.
ref_blocks: Word 24: the extra bits choose one of eight blocks
ref_w24_a: Device lists the valid final words: take the one whose BIP39 number lies in the block of your extra bits. Exactly one does.
ref_w24_b: Device accepts the final entropy bits (for example as coin flips): enter your three extra bits in order (1 = heads, 0 = tails where asked).
ref_w24_c: Otherwise: calculate word 24 with the lottabits command on an offline device.
ref_never_position: Never rely on the position of a word in the device’s list; always check its number in the booklet.
map_sub: One draw = one character. Write down the draw number, the character and its class.
pw_step_1: Mix the 88 chips. Draw one chip per character, note its number, put it back, mix.
pw_step_2: Look up each number in the character map; copy character and class.
pw_note: The draw numbers are the canonical record. If a character is hard to read, its number and class decide.
pp_booklet_sub: Open the page of the first draw, find the second draw: that word.
pp_step_1: Mix the 88 chips. Two draws per word, put each chip back and mix.
pp_step_2: Choose the word list before drawing and tick it below. Look up each coordinate in that list’s booklet.
quick_kit_text: An opaque bag (or a box with a hand opening, or a bingo cage), chips 01–88 that differ only in their number (65–88 may have another colour), these printables and a pen.
quick_step_1: Check the set on the inventory sheet before the session.
quick_step_2: Close the bag, shake it for about five seconds, reach into the middle without looking and draw one chip.
quick_step_4: Put it back: always with replacement. The next draw starts with shaking again.
quick_step_5: Draw unobserved: no cameras, no onlookers.
quick_seed_text: Chips 01–64. 46 draws → 23 words from the booklet, 3 extra bits, word 24 via hardware wallet or offline CLI. 256 bits.
quick_password_text: Chips 01–88. One draw per character from the character map. 12 characters ≈ 77.5 bits.
quick_passphrase_text: Chips 01–88. Two draws per word from the passphrase booklet. 6 words ≈ 77.5 bits.
quick_principle: The chips create secrets. The computer only calculates.
booklet_front_seed: BIP39 word numbers and words for chips 01–64
booklet_print_1: Print all pages double-sided on A4 at 100 % (actual size), flip on the short edge.
booklet_print_2: Without a duplex printer: print the odd pages first, put the printed stack back into the printer as your printer requires, then print the even pages.
booklet_print_3: Keep the sheets in order, fold the stack in the middle and staple it on the fold.
booklet_hash_note: Every page shows a data hash. The project documentation explains how to compare it with a trusted copy.
pp_use: The page number is the first draw. On that page, the second draw shows the word.
